chunks: He distributed their sustenance, and has counted their traces and their deeds, and numbered their breaths, and [knows] the darting of their eyes, and whatever their bosoms hide of the inner self, and their place of residence and their deposit in the loins and the wombs, until the limits are reached for them.

key_terms.خَائِنَةَ أَعْيُنِهِمْ: The darting of their eyes (indicating hidden thoughts)

ai.seo_question: What are the attributes of God regarding human sustenance and knowledge in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the context of Nahj al-Balagha’s enumeration of divine attributes, this passage underscores God’s absolute sovereignty over both the material and spiritual realms, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on divine omniscience (‘Ilm) and decree (Qadr). It emphasizes that God’s knowledge encompasses not only external actions but also the hidden intentions of the heart and the physical lineage from the womb to the grave, affirming His comprehensive control over human destiny.
